speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you have multiple skin lesions; can you tell me how long you have had them and if they are itchy, painful, or changing in size?

speaker: Patient
text: 2-year-old female. The patient's mother reports noticing multiple painless, nonpruritic papules on the child's abdomen. The child attends daycare where another child was reported to have similar lesions recently. Patient's brother had chickenpox one month ago. Immunizations are up-to-date.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the history. Given the daycare exposure and your brother's recent chickenpox, could you describe exactly what these papules look like and if you notice any blisters or crusts? Also, when did they first appear?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Skin-colored, nontender, pearly papules with central umbilication on the abdomen and extremities.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Molluscum Contagiosum. The description of pearly, umbilicated papules is pathognomonic, and the daycare exposure confirms the likely mode of transmission.
